summary: schema extra; shape official — vs generated type=object; external in the official YAML (TS28623_ComDefs.yaml); the generated document defines its own copy; 1 extra

answer.why_different: The generated document adds a local schema definition instead of using the externally defined ErrorResponse type. This is primarily a different address, with a structural consequence: the local definition is only an empty object and does not expose the external type's definition.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP evidence identifies ErrorResponse as a type defined in TS 28.623 and says it is used in error response bodies, but it does not provide the structure of ErrorResponse itself. Therefore, it does not establish whether this local empty-object copy is semantically complete or incorrect.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 permits reusable schemas in components and supports internal or external references. When a document is divided into connected parts, those parts must be referenced with $ref; however, the evidence does not establish whether this generated local schema replaces a required external reference or is merely an unused extra. Components have no effect unless referenced outside components.
answer.clearer_why: The official arrangement is easier to understand because it preserves the canonical external ErrorResponse definition identified by 3GPP, whereas the generated definition presents only an empty object and gives no information about the error payload's contents.

evidence.title: Relative References in URLs
evidence.text:
### Relative References in URLs  
Unless specified otherwise, all properties that are URLs MAY be relative references as defined by [RFC3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-4.2).
Relative references are resolved using the URLs defined in the [`Server Object`](#server-object) as a Base URI.  
Relative references used in `$ref` are processed as per [JSON Reference](https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-pbryan-zyp-json-ref-03), using the URL of the current document as the base URI. See also the [Reference Object](#reference-object).

evidence.query: $ref to a schema in another document ErrorResponseDefault
evidence.text:
```
MyResponseType:
oneOf:
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Lizard'
discriminator:
propertyName: pet_type
```  
The expectation now is that a property with name `pet_type` _MUST_ be present in the response payload, and the value will correspond to the name of a schema defined in the OAS document.  Thus the response payload:  
```
{
"id": 12345,
"pet_type": "Cat"
}
```  
Will indicate that the `Cat` schema be used in conjunction with this payload.  
In scenarios where the value of the discriminator field does not match the schema name or implicit mapping is not possible, an optional `mapping` definition MAY be used:  
```
MyResponseType:
oneOf:
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Dog'
- $ref: '#/components/schemas/Lizard'
- $ref: 'https://gigantic-server.com/schemas/Monster/schema.json'
discriminator:
propertyName: pet_type
mapping:
dog: '#/components/schemas/Dog'

evidence.title: Document Structure
evidence.text:
### Document Structure  
An OpenAPI document MAY be made up of a single document or be divided into multiple, connected parts at the discretion of the user. In the latter case, `$ref` fields MUST be used in the specification to reference those parts as follows from the [JSON Schema](http://json-schema.org) definitions.  
It is RECOMMENDED that the root OpenAPI document be named: `openapi.json` or `openapi.yaml`.
